cards.title: Breaking the quadratic color bound for bounded outdegree
cards.formal: Do there exist a constant ε∈(0,1], constants C₁,C₂>0, a computable function f:ℕ₊→ℕ₊ and one deterministic LOCAL algorithm that, for every n-vertex graph supplied with an orientation of maximum outdegree at most β≥1, computes a proper vertex coloring using at most ⌈C₁β^{2−ε}⌉ colors within f(β)+C₂log* n rounds?

cards.definitions: The communication network is a finite undirected simple graph G=(V,E), |V|=n≥2. Every edge has a supplied direction, known to its endpoints; no acyclicity is promised. A vertex’s outdegree is its number of outgoing edges, and every vertex has outdegree at most the supplied bound β. Its indegree and total degree may be arbitrarily large. A proper coloring assigns each vertex a label from one common palette so that endpoints of every edge have different labels, regardless of the edge direction. Vertices execute the same deterministic algorithm in synchronous rounds, have unique identifiers of O(log n) bits, know their incident ports and edge directions, and may know n and β. Each round allows a separate message of unbounded size to each neighbor in either direction and unrestricted finite local computation. Cost is worst-case round count over graphs, orientations and identifiers. No precomputed coloring or graph decomposition is supplied. The function f may grow arbitrarily fast with β, but cannot depend on n, total degree or the orientation’s path lengths. Both the exponent improvement ε and the coefficient of log* n must be uniform over β and n. Here log* n is the number of repeated base-two logarithms needed to reach a value at most one. Edgeless graphs, including the β=0 case, can be assigned one color separately.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the existence of the uniform deterministic algorithm with the stated palette and additive round bound, or establish that no such ε, constants, computable f and algorithm exist. A palette reduction by only logarithmic factors, a runtime depending on total degree, or a multiplicative log n term does not establish this claim.

cards.title: Characterizing countable patterns in monotone somewhere-dense hosts
cards.formal: Is there an explicit combinatorial characterization of the pairs (ℋ,𝒢) for which exact subgraph counting #Sub(ℋ→𝒢), parameterized by the number of pattern vertices, is fixed-parameter tractable, when 𝒢 is monotone and somewhere dense but ℋ is an arbitrary graph class? sentences: Count copies of a small input pattern inside a host graph, allowing extra edges between the copied vertices.
The goal is a structural criterion for runtime f(pattern size) times a polynomial with fixed exponent.
Hosts remain closed under subgraphs and somewhere dense, while the pattern class may be arbitrary.

cards.definitions: All graphs are finite, undirected and simple. The classes ℋ of patterns and 𝒢 of hosts are fixed for a counting problem; an input is a pair of explicitly represented graphs H∈ℋ and G∈𝒢, promised to belong to those classes. The parameter is k=|V(H)|. The output Sub(H,G) is the number of subgraphs of G isomorphic to H, not necessarily induced. Equivalently it is the number of injective maps V(H)→V(G) preserving every edge of H, divided by the number of automorphisms of H. Extra edges of G between image vertices need not be included in the counted subgraph. An automorphism is a vertex permutation preserving adjacency. Fixed-parameter tractability means an exact deterministic algorithm with runtime f(k)N^c for a computable f and a constant c, where N is the explicit input length. The algorithm, f and c may depend on the fixed pair of classes, but c cannot depend on k. Class membership is a promise, not part of the counting task. A host class is monotone if it is closed under deleting vertices and edges. It is somewhere dense if some fixed r≥0 has the property that, for every t, some graph in the class has K_t as an r-shallow minor: there are t pairwise disjoint connected vertex sets of radius at most r with an edge between every pair, whose contractions yield a clique after extra edges are discarded. A class is hereditary if it is closed under induced subgraphs. The source’s existing #Sub classification assumes hereditary ℋ; this question drops that assumption on ℋ while retaining monotonicity of 𝒢. The forbidden subgraphs of 𝒢 are the graphs not contained as subgraphs in any host in 𝒢; the sought criterion may depend on these host restrictions as well as on ℋ.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a precisely defined combinatorial condition on the two classes and prove that it is equivalent to fixed-parameter tractability in the stated setting, with its effectivity and complexity assumptions explicit. The source’s phrase “explicit combinatorial” still needs a formal admissibility convention. A classification only for hereditary patterns, a particular bounded-degeneracy host family, or one fixed finite pattern does not cover the requested scope.

cards.title: Do random CSPs and their spin glasses have the same overlap laws?
cards.formal: For a Boolean Max-CSP with random literal signs and its associated mixed Ising spin glass, do the distributions of the full overlap vectors of randomly chosen near-optimal solutions have limits as the number n of variables tends to infinity, and does the CSP limit tend to the spin-glass limit as the clause density α then tends to infinity? The source asks for this correspondence also for coupled collections of instances, but leaves the sampling and convergence conventions informal.
cards.why: Would strengthen the connection between random constraint optimization and spin glasses from optimal values and solution-space supports to the actual probability law of near-optimal geometry.
cards.status_note: The full conjecture and associated model definitions were read, the January 2023 arXiv revision checked, and later-result searches include the September 2026 RANDOM paper. No precise full-law resolution was located through 12 September 2026; the original convergence statement remains explicitly informal.

cards.definitions: For a fixed arity k and predicate f:{−1,+1}ᵏ→{0,1}, generate M independent constraints on n Boolean spins: each constraint chooses k variable indices independently and uniformly from {1,…,n}, allowing repetitions, and k independent uniform signs. Its value on σ is f(ε₁σᵢ₁,…,εₖσᵢₖ). Write α=M/n for the clause density and v(σ) for the fraction of constraints satisfied. The constant mean is μ=2^{−k}Σₓf(x). For S⊆{1,…,k}, the Fourier coefficient is f̂(S)=2^{−k}Σₓ f(x)∏ⱼ∈S xⱼ. Define aₚ=Σ_{|S|=p}f̂(S)² and ξ(t)=Σ_{p=1}^k aₚtᵖ. The corresponding spin-glass objective is Hξ(σ)=Σ_{p=1}^k √aₚ n^{−(p−1)/2}Σ_{i₁,…,iₚ=1}^n J^{(p)}_{i₁,…,iₚ}σᵢ₁⋯σᵢₚ, with all J entries independent standard normal variables. The CSP improvement over its mean is on the 1/√α scale, whereas Hξ/n has constant-order optimum. For ℓ configurations σ¹,…,σℓ, their full overlap vector Q has one coordinate for every I⊆{1,…,ℓ}: Q_I=n^{−1}Σ_{j=1}^n∏_{i∈I}σⁱⱼ. The empty product is one; two-element I give ordinary pairwise overlaps, and higher-order coordinates must not be discarded. Coupled ensembles permit correlations between instance objectives, as opposed to always taking independently generated instances. The intended comparison takes the large-n limit before the large-density limit; the source does not specify all additional limiting and solution-selection choices.
cards.answer_criterion: A complete formulation must fix the coupled instance law, near-optimal solution distribution and accuracy window, the mode of convergence and the order of every limit. The substantive target is convergence of the full probability laws of Q, or a refutation under those same conventions. Agreement only of optimal values, attainable overlap supports or forbidden overlap regions does not establish equality of probability laws.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
